findings.description: map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPs to any instance launched in this subnet, increasing exposure to the internet and expanding attack surface for instances that may not need direct public access.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPs to instances launched in this subnet, which combined with the internet gateway route creates unnecessary public exposure of resources placed here.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true (nor a kms_key_id), so data stored on this volume, which is attached to the portal server instance, is unencrypted at rest.

A default route (0.0.0.0/0) to the internet gateway is associated with the route table used by both public subnets, which combined with map_public_ip_on_launch exposes any attached instances directly to the internet without network segmentation.

AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the user_data startup script, exposing long-lived IAM credentials to anyone with access to instance metadata, the Terraform state, or console/API describe-instance calls.
The security group allows inbound TCP port 22 (SSH) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the management interface of the instance to the entire internet.
The security group allows inbound TCP port 80 from 0.0.0.0/0 with no compensating controls (e.g., no TLS/HTTPS), exposing the web service broadly and only over plaintext HTTP.
The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration, leaving potentially sensitive network traffic metadata stored unencrypted.

findings.issue_category: missing access controls / public access block
findings.description: The bucket has no public access block or bucket policy restricting access, and force_destroy is enabled, increasing risk that flow log data could be exposed or accidentally deleted without safeguard.

The snapshot is created from aws_ebs_volume.portal_server_disk without any visibility into whether the source volume is encrypted; if the source volume lacks encryption, this snapshot will also store data at rest unencrypted, and snapshots of this type are easy to share/copy publicly, increasing exposure risk of sensitive data.
